about: MMB-by-MMB against the authors' code on the paper's four networks with hidden nodes, at the paper's named targets; FCI and RFCI read at each target and the IAMB blanket arm are context. The release summary's MMB-by-MMB entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 14 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch with mmb_by_mmb as merged and the lane's paper targets); the judged fits ran just before the merge of its smaller-blanket search's last commits, and the merged build gave the same marks and test counts at all 1,040 fits
hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor for most fits, and AMD EPYC 9534, AMD EPYC 9555, and Intel Xeon nodes for the rest, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; the authors' code, FCI, and RFCI ran in one run and Andrey's fits in another, each on shared nodes, so the times are indicative
verdict_rule: per cell (network, rows; 20 datasets, the paper's named targets): per dataset, the mean over the targets with a true edge of the distance of the precision and recall of the edges at the target from (1, 1) and of their F1, an edge right only with both marks right (an answer with no edge counts precision 1, distance 1, F1 0); D = Andrey's minus the authors' code's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree
error_metric: edge_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the precision and recall of the edges at the target from (1, 1), an edge right only with both endpoint marks right; edge_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of their F1. The floor uses the local endpoint SHD at the target (extra, missing, and mismarked edges) against the empty answer's, the target's true degree
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, one target per fit, no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit (3,600 s on WIN95PTS at 5,000 rows, the largest cell), past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out
seeds_note: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; a rerun holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39
cells_note: the paper's four networks (MILDEW, ALARM, WIN95PTS, ANDES) as linear-Gaussian models, weights +-U(0.5, 1), N(0, 1) noise, 4/4/6/10 random non-target nodes hidden, columns shuffled; the truth is the PAG of the observed variables, read at each target
comparisons_note: judged: Andrey against the authors' code; context, reported and never judged: Andrey's FCI and pcalg's RFCI read at each target, and mmb_by_mmb with blanket='iamb' (MILDEW and ALARM)
